evals.prompt: I want to create a new Spice.ai Cloud app called 'analytics-prod' in the US West region, add a database secret, and deploy it. Walk me through the API calls.
evals.expected_output: Step-by-step: list regions, POST /v1/projects with region us-west-2 (legacy /v1/apps also works), POST secrets, POST deployments, check status

assertions.name: creates_app
assertions.description: Should show creating the project via API (canonical /v1/projects or legacy /v1/apps)

evals.prompt: How do I rotate my Spice.ai Cloud API keys without any downtime for my clients?
evals.expected_output: Use the dual-key system: regenerate secondary, update clients, then regenerate primary

assertions.name: explains_dual_key
assertions.description: Should explain the dual-key rotation system

evals.prompt: My Spice.ai Cloud project 123 runs in us-east-1. Make a copy of it in us-west-2 called analytics-west, with the same datasets, connections, and secrets, and get it running.
evals.expected_output: Fork the project with POST /v1/projects/123/forks and {"name": "analytics-west", "region": "us-west-2"} instead of recreating it by hand, check shared_state in the response, then deploy the fork with POST /v1/projects/{forkId}/deployments because a fork is not deployed on creation

assertions.name: forks_project
assertions.description: Should fork the source project rather than recreate it

assertions.name: targets_region
assertions.description: Should place the fork in us-west-2

assertions.name: deploys_fork
assertions.description: Should deploy the fork, which forking does not do

assertions.name: checks_shared_state
assertions.description: Should check the settings the fork shares with its source before deploying

evals.prompt: Update existing monitor 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222 on our managed Spice Cloud project 123. It uses query_latency_p99; change its threshold to 2500 ms and notify both oncall@example.com and Slack channel C0123ABCD. Keep its other condition settings and enabled state. Slack is connected. Show the Management API requests and how you verify the update. Do not recreate the alert.
evals.expected_output: GET the existing UUID, preserve its enabled state and other spec fields, PATCH that same monitor with the complete modified spec and the email plus Slack targets array, then GET again to verify. Requires monitors:write and org admin. Does not delete/recreate or claim delivery from PATCH success.

assertions.name: uses_patch
assertions.description: Updates the existing monitor rather than replacing it

assertions.name: same_monitor_route
assertions.description: Uses the original project and alert ID

assertions.name: multiple_destinations
assertions.description: Uses the full targets array for email and Slack

assertions.name: admin_role
assertions.description: States the monitor update role requirement

expectations: Reads the current alert and uses its complete spec rather than resetting window, sustain, or severity defaults
Preserves status instead of enabling a disabled alert without approval
Reads back the same UUID after PATCH and verifies threshold plus both destinations
Does not send DELETE or POST to recreate the existing monitor
Does not treat enabled configuration or successful PATCH as proof of evaluation or notification delivery

evals.prompt: Our managed Spice Cloud project 123 has accelerated sales.orders and sales.customers datasets and an OpenAI model. Set up an Error-state monitor for both datasets, refresh-error monitoring, and model-failure monitoring using the Management API. Explain units and prerequisites. Our CPU monitor is active but GET says evaluation_unavailable_reason is cpu_limit_missing. Is it healthy? Can I use the Management Bearer token to send a test notification and read episode history?
evals.expected_output: All three requested templates are released for appropriately configured managed projects. Dataset status uses EQ 3 with a datasets list supporting dotted names, refresh errors count recorded errors per window, and current LLM failures use a per-second rate. Missing CPU limit means it cannot evaluate, not healthy. Test notifications and episode history are portal-session features, not public /v1 routes. Distinguishes pending #5634 changes from shipped behavior.

assertions.name: multiple_datasets
assertions.description: Scopes the Error-state monitor to both datasets

assertions.name: cpu_observation_gap
assertions.description: Explains unavailable evaluation separately from enabled state

expectations: Does not claim llm_failures, dataset_refresh_errors, or dataset_status requires early access
Uses EQ threshold 3 for Error and both dotted dataset names
Distinguishes refresh-error counts from current request-failure rate units
Does not claim CPU is healthy because its configuration is active
Does not invent public /v1 test, events, observation-state, or catalog endpoints
Requests consent before real test notifications and asks recipients to confirm arrival
